chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard a man saying to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! I am a man who has aged, and I have married a young virgin, and I have not yet entered upon her. I fear that when I enter upon her on my bed, she will dislike me due to my dye (hair color) and my old age.'

So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When you go in, instruct them before she comes to you that she should be in a state of wudu. Then you should not approach her until you have performed wudu and prayed two rak'at.'
Then glorify Allah, and send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Then supplicate to Allah, and instruct those with her to say 'Ameen' to your supplication.

And say: 'O Allah! Grant me her affection, her love, and her pleasure, and make me pleased with her. Then unite us with the best of unions and the most intimate of alliances, for You love the permissible and dislike the forbidden.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And know that affection (al-ilf) is from Allah, and separation (al-firk) is from Satan, so that he may make disliked that which Allah has permitted.'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals and supplications for a husband to seek his wife's affection and unity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) provides a spiritual remedy for marital anxiety, prescribing a specific sequence of purification, prayer, and supplication to foster *ilf* (affection) and *wudd* (love). This practice highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating physical intimacy with spiritual mindfulness, ensuring that the union is blessed and free from the distractions of Satan. The theological conclusion underscores that true marital harmony is a divine gift, contrasting it with the discord (*firak*) instigated by Satan to make the permissible seem repulsive.
